Hi Sara / Anna — thanks for the patience. Per internal review:

1) Subprocessors: attached CSV reflects current list; no EU-only new providers beyond the planned lightweight edge cache POC (Dublin/Frankfurt) targeted for late April. We will provide a one-time notification ahead of launch. (Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessors_2026-02-10.csv)

2) SCCs & UK IDTA: Redwood will adopt the EU Controller-Processor SCCs and is willing to sign the UK IDTA addendum. Markus has provided narrow counterlanguage (attached below) to tidy the IDTA carve-outs around notice cadence and our commercial warranty cap.

3) Transfer-impact language: proposed paragraph below (final wording attached as a tracked change in the counter DPA):

"Where transfers are made pursuant to EU SCCs or the UK IDTA, Redwood maintains a documented transfer impact assessment and implements technical and organizational measures proportionate to the risk, including encryption at rest and in transit, dedicated KMS key separation, access controls, and logging/audit capabilities. Redwood shall notify the controller of any legally binding request for disclosure by a public authority to the extent permitted. Redwood does not warrant the outcome of sovereign requests and will engage in reasonable cooperation with the controller where lawful to do so."

4) Execution: we can proceed with DocuSign once ThermoAI confirms acceptance of the IDTA addendum with the narrow carve-outs. Suggested execution flow: both parties sign the final DPA and separately sign the UK IDTA addendum in the same envelope (two documents). DocuSign envelope prepared: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/details/0123456789abcdef

If you confirm, we'll upload the final tracked-change DPA and the IDTA addendum to the envelope and request signatures.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
